title: Practical tips for working a conference crowd
why: Join conversations by standing nearby and nodding, then contribute only when you have something intelligent to add. Never crash private events.

title: Internal memo on outage and public criticism
why: Corporate memo defending the company after an outage and press coverage; no technical lesson.

title: Shipping costs erased a shrink-wrap startup's margin
why: Shipping from Michigan to the Caribbean tripled landed costs, so a healthy per-square-foot markup still could not make the business work.

title: Defending XML against common criticisms
why: XML verbosity comes from end tags and angle brackets inherited from SGML, and binary data needs safe text encoding for interchange.

title: Argument about music, concerts and technology
why: Opinion-driven rebuttal about music habits and the Idiocracy film; no technical takeaway.

title: Facebook team conflicts and press access
why: Opinionated commentary on internal team conflicts and journalists; cut off and lacks a concrete lesson.

title: Living abroad while running a startup
why: Personal lifestyle account of relocating for visa limits; no transferable technical or factual lesson.

title: How Amazon fee-based price parity raises prices
why: Sellers paying 30 to 45 percent fees and being punished for cheaper offers elsewhere raises prices across the board, not just on Amazon.

title: Narrative about a cooperative maze game
why: Fun play-by-play of emergent cooperation in a game; no lesson that stands on its own.

title: How big-tech hiring committees make decisions
why: Committee rejections often mean not hired this round, leveling deadlocks are common, and recruiters' relayed reasons are often distorted.

title: SSH offers every public key to any server
why: SSH sends your public keys to each server it tries, so servers can see them and possibly link them to public GitHub keys.

title: Negotiating by anchoring on top-line salary
why: Keep perks like relocation and vacation as bargaining chips to trade away, while holding firm on the headline salary number.

title: Accusations against an Oxford vaccine team
why: Unsupported accusations and reputational attacks against researchers; no verifiable technical content.

title: GADTs explained: type-refining constructors in Haskell
why: Algebraic data types combine sums and products; GADTs let each constructor refine the type index, enabling type-safe evaluators for ASTs.

title: Critique of Java's primitive and object design
why: Opinionated rant against Java's design choices; it makes a design argument but mostly expresses dislike without evidence.

title: Speculation on state policy and re-education
why: Political speculation about a government policy; not a technical or informational lesson.

title: Promotion of a free deep learning course
why: Self-promotional pitch for a course with testimonials; little learning content on its own.

title: Why stealth buys time rather than invisibility
why: Stealth delays detection; coatings tune one radar band, leaving early-warning MHz and Ka-band radars and IR cues exposed.

title: Rebuttal to a business advice post
why: Argumentative response about sales hiring and business philosophy; a debate, not an explanation.

title: Reflections on rereading one's own old code
why: Personal reflection on code quality and thinking time; generic opinion without concrete technical substance.

title: Why small social lies set workplace tone
why: Opinion and personal anecdote about greetings and negativity at work; no concrete teachable method.

title: Commentary on a GitHub departure controversy
why: Commentary on a contested personnel story; speculative and not informative on its own.

title: Practical GCC inline assembly conventions for AVX2
why: Use symbolic operand names in upper case, one input per line with comments, and constraints like +&x for early-clobber vector registers.

title: Why ARM sued Qualcomm over Nuvia's licensed IP
why: Nuvia's ARM license required approval for IP transfers, so ARM sought control to block licensees from later dropping its architecture.

title: Essay on Franzen and modern society
why: Opinion essay on social media, competition and society; no technical lesson.

title: Back-of-envelope scale of replacing fossil energy
why: Replacing fuel-based transport needs over a thousand 1 GW plants by this estimate, and home solar rarely covers EV charging plus cooling.

title: Why P=NP would not mean practical algorithms
why: A polynomial-time algorithm can have huge exponents, so proving P=NP would not automatically make NP-complete problems practically easy.

title: Personal story of a Soviet-era exchange program
why: Personal immigration and high-school anecdote with no transferable lesson.

title: Personal story of building a voxel game
why: Autobiographical account of a long game project; motivational rather than instructive.

title: Cognitive fundamentals before considering supplements
why: Hydration, sleep consolidating memory from hippocampus to neocortex, and exercise support cognition before any supplements are considered.

title: Personal take on Knockout.js bindings
why: Subjective praise for a framework's clarity; a preference rather than a transferable explanation.

title: Normit transforms and why deep nets are hard to debug
why: Quantile-to-Gaussian normit transforms often boost power over nonparametric tests; stacked ReLU layers act as chained regressions that are hard to debug.

title: Rebuttal to Zinsser on clear writing
why: Snarky rebuttal of a writing guide's examples; mostly contrarian tone rather than instruction.

title: Why per-phone royalties favor premium phone makers
why: Royalties tied to device price make identical cellular tech costlier on high-end phones, giving Apple a strong reason to negotiate hard.

title: Meta-analysis of which hiring methods predict performance
why: Schmidt and Hunter's 1998 meta-analysis summarizes which selection methods, such as interviews and tests, actually predict job performance.

title: Bing Chat generated jokes about the Three Stooges
why: Entertainment samples of AI-generated jokes; no informational content.

title: Rebuttal to a post about women in tech
why: Argumentative rebuttal of a provocation; rhetorical rather than explanatory.

title: Argument about why men get hired over women
why: Opinion argument with unsupported generalizations about gender and hiring.

title: Why early Netflix content was cheap to license
why: Studios licensed content cheaply before realizing streaming would displace cable and DVDs, which explains Netflix's early value proposition.

title: What Anthos actually is, broken into components
why: Anthos GKE runs clusters beyond Google Cloud, and many Anthos features are available separately under different product names.

title: Runescape's gold economy and farming as income
why: The Grand Exchange order book made in-game item prices volatile, so farming gold became a market exposed to price swings.

title: Opinion on PostgreSQL's distribution gaps
why: Argument about PostgreSQL versus other databases; the points are opinion without concrete explanation.

title: Learn sysadmin basics before running Docker in production
why: Docker is an optimization, not a substitute for Linux, networking, backups and security skills; production needs automated provisioning and deploys.

title: Rant calling bitcoin a ponzi scheme
why: Polemic against bitcoin and its supporters; opinion without substantive analysis.

title: Humorous essay on airplane smoking bans
why: Light humorous essay with minor history; no substantive explanation.

title: Defense of programmers against a cheap jab
why: Opinion and rhetoric defending programmers; no technical lesson.

title: Why Mario 64 rendering was bound by N64 microcode
why: N64 games built command lists for RSP microcode and used mandated matrix libraries, so optimizations depended on the microcode team's revisions.

title: Personal account of learning Clojure
why: Subjective account of learning curve and enthusiasm; little concrete explanation.

title: Opinion on youth services and suicide
why: Emotional opinion about youth services and suicide; no verifiable informational lesson.

title: When genetic algorithms are actually a good fit
why: GAs suit specific classes of objective functions; judge them against competing optimizers on speed rather than trusting biological analogies.

title: Why modern motherboards replace many PCIe cards
why: Current motherboards include many USB ports, M.2 WiFi slots and multi-gigabit NICs, making many add-in cards unnecessary.

title: Function pointers: dispatch tables and callbacks
why: Function pointers let libraries call user policy at runtime, replacing big switch statements with O(1) dispatch and enabling extensible callbacks.

title: Personal laptop shopping criteria in the UK
why: Personal buying checklist tied to UK prices and dated models; not generalizable.

title: Insider story behind SimCopter's easter egg
why: The unapproved content, not the bug, got its developer fired, and the delay pushed SimCopter past the holiday season.

title: Why undocumented startup partnerships can still be joint ventures
why: Joint ventures are a form of partnership law, so a missing written agreement does not prevent a court from finding one with ownership claims.

title: Personal request for work during family crisis
why: Personal request for help and venting; no technical lesson.

title: Why LCD ghosting varies by panel supplier
why: Every OEM panel maker has ghosting issues, Apple cannot change panel physics, and LiPo battery fires are rare despite viral videos.

title: Why many VCs refuse to sign NDAs
why: NDAs create conflicts across portfolios, so VCs rely on reputation and founders withhold secrets until background checks are done.

title: Critique of startup cargo cult advice
why: Satirical critique of startup clichés; opinion rather than explanation.

title: Static generics versus dynamic trait objects in Rust
why: Generic bounds generate a copy per type at compile time; dyn trait objects dispatch at runtime, so prefer generics unless you need mixed collections.

title: How big companies misuse startup trade secrets
why: Promising a firewall then passing secrets across it is blatant misappropriation, and startups dependent on one big partner face severe risk.

title: Scaling a web stack one bottleneck at a time
why: Load balancing, read replicas, sharding, memcached and reverse proxy caches each answer a specific bottleneck that appears as load grows.

title: Opinion that early returns are harmful
why: Strong opinion against early returns with anecdotal claims; argument rather than an explanation.

title: Critique of Facebook's public statement wording
why: Adversarial reading of a corporate statement; opinion and rhetoric rather than verifiable information.

title: Experienced dev finds AI code needs heavy rewriting
why: On a 15-year-old Java and React system, AI-generated code often needed about 70 percent rewriting after self-review because of architecture issues.

title: Treat leap seconds like timezone offset changes
why: Store timestamps in TAI and apply leap seconds as offset changes, like DST, avoiding the repeated-second ambiguity of UTC.

title: Speculation on Y Combinator admissions
why: Speculative opinion about YC applicants and selection; no verifiable explanation.

title: Personal account of quitting Facebook and Twitter
why: Personal anecdote and opinion about social media habits; no technical lesson.

title: Meta-commentary on a gender debate
why: Summary of a heated debate with no substantive explanation of its own.

title: Argument defining tacos and burritos
why: Cultural and culinary opinion about food definitions; not technical or factual learning.

title: Rant about Ctrl key conventions on Linux
why: Emotional rant about copy and paste conventions; the tool recommendation is only a passing mention.

title: Complaints about pushy digital advertising
why: Opinion about ad annoyance and a wish for standardized ads; no substantive analysis.

title: Argument against energy-intensive crypto
why: Political opinion about crypto externalities and energy; argument without technical explanation.

title: Geopolitical argument about sanctions on Russia
why: Contested political opinion about sanctions and Ukraine; not an informational explanation.

title: Personal list of reasons to dislike SF
why: Subjective personal list about cost, transit and parking; anecdotal preferences rather than transferable insight.

title: Why high-APR loans are dischargeable in US bankruptcy
why: US bankruptcy generally discharges high-APR loans while student loans usually are not, which shapes how lenders price risk.

title: Argument about the word sexual assault
why: Opinion arguing about terminology for airport screening incidents; not informative.

title: Commentary on the UK Socialist Workers Party
why: Political commentary about a UK party and its ban; opinion without a technical lesson.

title: Why Verilog's imperative style mismatches hardware
why: Verilog and VHDL inherit imperative C and Ada models for inherently parallel circuits, while functional tools like Clash fit hardware better.

title: Advocacy for tokens and cryptonetworks
why: Advocacy piece on tokens and permissionless networks; argument rather than explanation.

title: Personal account of eating hakarl and whale
why: Personal taste experience with no broader lesson.

title: Why ship steering and speed should share one controller
why: Splitting control across roles and hidden backup modes causes mode confusion; unified controls prevent the mismatch behind ship collisions.

title: How the pre-2017 SAT's difficulty ordering affected strategy
why: Questions rise in difficulty within sections, so returning to skipped items can cost time, and the ungraded section works as a planned break.

title: Anecdote on Lisbon rents and property income
why: Personal observations and opinion about housing markets; not a substantiated explanation.

title: Why Shenzhen's dense supplier cluster speeds up hardware
why: Fabs, mold shops and distributors within 2km enable cheap rapid prototyping, and apparent redundancy carries collective learning across suppliers.

title: Opinion on QSBS and tax proposals
why: Political opinion about tax policy and equity taxation; no informational explanation.

title: Quoted moderator story about re-uploaded videos
why: Mostly quoted article material with brief reaction; no analysis or method.

title: Spotify's original native client and why it was fast
why: The early desktop app used a custom-rendered UI and an optimized protocol, a responsiveness edge lost when it later moved to a Chromium wrapper.

title: Power Distance Index and workplace directness
why: Low power distance cultures reward blunt communication while high ones prefer diplomacy, so the same phrasing reads differently across national work cultures.

title: How zoning rules block small storefronts
why: Even a tiny cafe can require architects, elevators and sprinklers under zoning, pushing cities toward chain-only commercial space.

title: Questions for valuing a money-losing ride-share IPO
why: Compare valuation multiples rather than absolute size, and ask what path turns rising revenue with rising losses into profit.

title: Complaint that iPad Pro lacks real use cases
why: Subjective product complaint about iPad software limits; opinion without deeper explanation.

title: Proposal for personal control over feed algorithms
why: Design opinion about executive control over social feeds; a proposal without substantiation.

title: Moral argument about developers abandoning projects
why: Opinion on duty and abandoned projects; moral argument rather than informative content.

title: Why zero marginal cost does not make digital goods free
why: Digital goods have high fixed costs and zero marginal cost, so creators still need revenue, much like a train that costs the same whether full or empty.

title: Response in a dispute about an expat recruiter
why: Defensive reply in a personal and business dispute; no general lesson.

title: Opinion on Brexit consequences for Europe
why: Political speculation about Brexit's effects; opinion rather than substantiated explanation.

title: Complaints about Facebook feed and friends
why: Subjective complaints about social media behavior; no technical or factual lesson.

title: Null references versus logical missing-value sentinels
why: Hoare's criticism targets null references, not logical missing values; without nulls, programmers reinvent them with flags or sentinel values.

title: Five levels of language proficiency and social integration
why: Professional fluency does not guarantee social fluency; friendships need passive comprehension of fast, slang-heavy group conversations.
